fields.rationale: AHB and APB are NOT opcode/byte-oriented command protocols. They are address-and-control bus protocols. The 'commands' are encoded as multi-bit field tuples driven by the Manager during the address phase (AHB) or setup phase (APB), together with a transfer-type indicator (HTRANS / PSEL+PENABLE).

ahb_transfer_type_encoding_HTRANS.0b00: IDLE   - no data transfer; Subordinate must give zero-wait OKAY; transfer must be ignored
ahb_transfer_type_encoding_HTRANS.0b01: BUSY   - Manager continuing a burst but next transfer cannot occur yet; Subordinate must give zero-wait OKAY; transfer must be ignored
ahb_transfer_type_encoding_HTRANS.0b10: NONSEQ - single transfer or first transfer of a burst (address unrelated to previous)
ahb_transfer_type_encoding_HTRANS.0b11: SEQ    - subsequent burst transfer (address related to previous)

ahb_burst_type_encoding_HBURST.0b001: INCR    - incrementing burst of undefined length

ahb_response_encoding_HRESP.1: ERROR - access failed (two-cycle response: HRESP=1+HREADY=0, then HRESP=1+HREADY=1)

ahb_protection_HPROT_extended_AHB5.HPROT[6]: 0 Non-shareable / 1 Shareable (must be 0 for Device memory)

ahb_secure_signaling_AHB5.HNONSEC: 0 = Secure transfer (default), 1 = Non-secure transfer. Address-phase signal; must remain constant throughout a burst. Supported only if AHB5 Secure_Transfers property is True.

ahb_exclusive_signaling_AHB5.HEXCL: Manager output, 1 = transfer is part of an Exclusive Access sequence (supported only if AHB5 Exclusive_Transfers property is True)
ahb_exclusive_signaling_AHB5.HMASTER: Manager identifier (HMASTER_WIDTH 0..8 bits) used by the Exclusive Access Monitor
ahb_exclusive_signaling_AHB5.HEXOKAY: Subordinate output, 1 = success of an Exclusive Transfer; 0 = failure (another Manager wrote the monitored address)

SETUP.transition: Unconditional -> ACCESS on next rising PCLK

apb_protection_PPROT_encoding_APB4.PPROT[1]: 0 = secure access, 1 = non-secure access (Non-secure convention: HIGH = Non-secure)

apb_pslverr_mapping_to_AHB_AXI.AXI-to-APB: PSLVERR maps back to RRESP/BRESP = SLVERR (RRESP[1]/BRESP[1]).

ahb_locked_access_sequence: Manager asserts HMASTLOCK=1 with the start of a non-IDLE transfer; the bus locks once HMASTLOCK is asserted while HSEL is asserted and HREADY=HIGH.
All transfers in the locked sequence must address the same Subordinate region.
Manager deasserts HMASTLOCK when the sequence is complete; the bus unlocks on the cycle with HMASTLOCK=0 and HREADY=HIGH.
Recommendation: insert an IDLE transfer immediately after a locked sequence.
ahb_exclusive_access_sequence_AHB5: Manager issues an Exclusive Read (HEXCL=1) with a Manager ID on HMASTER to address X.
Subordinate records (X, HMASTER) in its Exclusive Access Monitor; returns OKAY with HEXOKAY=1.
Manager later issues an Exclusive Write (HEXCL=1, same HMASTER) to address X.
If no other Manager wrote to X in between: Subordinate updates memory, returns HEXOKAY=1.
If another Manager wrote to X: Subordinate does NOT update memory, returns HEXOKAY=0.
valid_ready_handshake_rules_ahb: HREADY is a global Data-phase signal driven by the multiplexor (combining all Subordinate HREADYOUTs).
A Subordinate must sample its inputs (HSELx, address, control) only when HREADY=HIGH (indicating previous transfer is completing).
Each Subordinate drives HREADYOUT only during the data phase of a transfer that selected it.
There is no master-side READY in AHB; the Manager must accept HRDATA whenever HREADY goes HIGH for a read.
Strict 1-cycle address phase: address-phase signals are not waited (they are driven for one HCLK cycle unless extended by the previous data phase's HREADY=LOW).
valid_ready_handshake_rules_apb: PSELx + PENABLE jointly indicate the transfer state (00=IDLE, 10=SETUP, 11=ACCESS).
PREADY drives wait states only in the ACCESS phase (PENABLE=1).
PREADY can take any value while PENABLE=LOW (a peripheral with fixed-2-cycle access may tie PREADY HIGH).
The Manager (bridge) holds PADDR, PWRITE, PSELx, PWDATA, PSTRB, PPROT stable while PREADY=LOW.
fields.single_response_for_burst_ahb: Each beat of an AHB burst gets its own HRESP. An ERROR on any beat allows the Manager to cancel the remaining transfers in the burst (HTRANS=IDLE during the two-cycle ERROR). Burst transfers do not have a single grouped response (unlike AXI BRESP).
fields.per_beat_response_for_read_ahb: HRESP is per-beat on the read response path; the Subordinate may give per-beat ERROR responses for the same burst.

evidence.spec_section: 1.1 About the protocol — Manager / Subordinate / Interconnect
evidence.quote: A Manager provides address and control information to initiate read and write operations. ... A Subordinate responds to transfers initiated by Managers in the system. The Subordinate uses the HSELx select signal from the decoder to control when it responds to a bus transfer.
HBURST[2:0]: 0b000 SINGLE, 0b001 INCR, 0b010 WRAP4, 0b011 INCR4, 0b100 WRAP8, 0b101 INCR8, 0b110 WRAP16, 0b111 INCR16.
HPROT[0] 0=Opcode fetch / 1=Data access; HPROT[1] 0=User access / 1=Privileged access; HPROT[2] 0=Non-bufferable / 1=Bufferable; HPROT[3] 0=Non-cacheable / 1=Cacheable (Modifiable in Issue B/C).

evidence.spec_section: Table 3-7 Permitted combinations of HPROT bits (Memory type)
evidence.quote: HPROT[6:2] -> Device-nE / Device-E / Normal Non-cacheable / Write-through / Write-back, with Non-shareable or Shareable variants.
When LOW, the HRESP signal indicates that the transfer status is OKAY. When HIGH, the HRESP signal indicates that the transfer status is ERROR. ERROR response is a two-cycle response.

PCLK Clock; PRESETn Reset (active LOW, normally connected directly to system bus reset); PADDR Address (up to 32 bits); PPROT Protection type; PSELx Select per peripheral; PENABLE Enable (second and subsequent cycles of an APB transfer); PWRITE Direction (HIGH = write, LOW = read); PWDATA Write data; PSTRB Write strobes (one per 8 bits); PREADY Ready (slave extends transfer); PRDATA Read data; PSLVERR Failure indicator.
PPROT[0] 1 = privileged access / 0 = normal access; PPROT[1] 1 = nonsecure access / 0 = secure access; PPROT[2] 1 = instruction access / 0 = data access.

From AXI to APB: an APB error is mapped back to RRESP/BRESP = SLVERR. From AHB to APB: PSLVERR is mapped back to HRESP = ERROR for both reads and writes; this is achieved by mapping PSLVERR to the AHB signal HRESP[0].
